A 5-minute practice

Evening reflection

Three foundations of Right Action

In early Buddhist teaching, ethical conduct begins with restraint. In daily life, restraint becomes care.

01

Protect life

Choose actions that reduce intentional harm to people, animals, and yourself.

02

Take only what is given

Respect property, time, credit, attention, and the trust another person places in you.

03

Honor boundaries

Let consent, honesty, responsibility, and care guide intimate relationships.

History note: no surviving record tells us what the Buddha did on every calendar date. Dates for his life are debated. Each entry therefore pairs a broadly chronological episode from traditional biographies with a present-day practice; it is reflection, not a literal 2,500-year-old diary.
